chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub narrated from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who marries off his female slave to a man and stipulates upon him that every child she bears will be free. Her husband then divorces her, and she marries another man and bears a child. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he wishes, he frees her; and if he wishes, he does not free her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a female slave if she bears a child to a new husband after being divorced by the first?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal mechanism of *Umm al-Walad* (mother of the child) status, specifically addressing the scenario where a conditional manumission clause is fulfilled by a subsequent husband after a divorce. It highlights the juristic principle that the right to confirm or withhold the emancipation of the mother rests with the current owner, reflecting the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the completion of manumission conditions. This ruling underscores the importance of contractual stipulations (*shurut*) in determining the final status of a slave woman within the household.
